title: The Time Nazis Invaded Florida
summary: Hosts Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant recount Operation Pastorius, the 1942 Nazi sabotage mission in which eight German saboteurs landed by U-boat on Long Island (Amagansett, NY) and Ponte Vedra Beach, Florida. They cover the selection and training of the men, their explosive targets, the betrayal by team leader George Dasch, the FBI's manhunt and J. Edgar Hoover's credit-taking, the military tribunal, six electrocutions in Washington D.C., the commutations of Dasch and Burger, and a later failed landing in Maine. The episode opens with tour announcements and closes with a listener mail segment from a parent whose toddler loves the show.
topics: Ponte Vedra Beach Florida Nazi landing
Nazi plan to bomb New York

segments.title: Tour thanks and opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts thank fans for the Northeast summer tour and tease fall Midwest dates, then introduce the topic of Nazi saboteurs who invaded America in World War II.

segments.title: Hitler's plan to strike New York
segments.summary: Hitler's desire to destroy New York, V-2 rocket and long-range bomber ideas, and his decision to send saboteurs after the attack on Pearl Harbor. The sabotage unit of German Military Intelligence is introduced.

segments.title: Selecting the saboteurs and the American Bund
segments.summary: Walter Kappe selects Operation Pastorius leaders using emigration records and American Bund members, many of them former Nazi Party members. The team of eight is split into two groups of four.

segments.title: Profiles of Team Dasch and Team Burger
segments.summary: Biographies of George Dasch, who had lived in America and was picked for being American-seeming, and Ernst Burger, a early Nazi who fled to the US, served in the National Guard, returned to Germany, and was imprisoned.

segments.title: Team Kerling and the rest of the recruits
segments.summary: Profiles of Edward Kerling, a former butler and cook who tried to sail back to Germany, Herbert Haupt, the youngest member, and the remaining recruits. Only two of the original twelve had military experience.

segments.title: Training and assigned targets
segments.summary: The men receive eighteen days of training in explosives and sabotage at a camp, then are assigned targets including Niagara Falls hydroelectric plants, aluminum plants, Ohio River locks, railroad sites, and New York's water supply, along with general terrorism aims.

segments.title: U-boat landings in Florida and Long Island
segments.summary: Two U-boats carry the teams, with explosives and about a million dollars in today's value in cash. Team Dasch lands on Long Island near Amagansett, buries explosives, and is spotted by Coast Guardsman John Cullen, whom Dasch bribes with $260 before he leaves. Team Kerling lands in Ponte Vedra Beach, Florida.

segments.title: Discovery of buried explosives and the FBI response
segments.summary: The buried explosives are found and reported to NYPD Captain John Bayliss, who alerts the FBI. Within thirteen hours the FBI has the materials and Hoover seeks a news blackout. The hosts describe the saboteurs' early movements in New York and Chicago.

segments.title: Dasch betrays the mission
segments.summary: Dasch summons Burger, offers him the choice to join or be thrown out the window, and they agree to betray the plan. Dasch plays pinochle, travels to Washington, calls the FBI, and is picked up and interviewed by Mickey Ladd. Team members are tracked and arrested, and Hoover claims credit for the case in a letter to Roosevelt.

segments.title: Military tribunal, executions, and clemency
segments.summary: Roosevelt sets up a military tribunal in Washington, D.C., prosecuted by Francis Biddle. Six saboteurs are electrocuted at the D.C. jail on August 8. Dasch and Burger are spared; Truman commutes their sentences and they are deported to Germany. Dasch later tries to clear his name and fades from the public eye.

segments.title: Later German landing attempt in Maine
segments.summary: A later German submarine landed two German American saboteurs in a snowstorm off Maine, where a Boy Scout spotted them and alerted police. The hosts note this was apparently the last such attempt.

segments.title: Listener mail: a toddler who loves the show
segments.summary: A listener named Shawna shares an audio clip of her two-and-a-half-year-old son Archer asking to listen to Stuff You Should Know at nap time. The hosts respond warmly.

segments.title: Sign-off and contact info
segments.summary: The hosts give social media, email, and website details and sign off.
